# Radio

One choice in a `RadioGroup`, with its label to its right. Pass the choices as the group's `options` unless you need a layout they cannot express, such as a choice with a rich description; then render `Radio` children.

```tsx
import { Radio } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/radio-group/radio-group";
```

## Example

```tsx
<RadioGroup legend="Size" name="size">
  <Radio value="small" label="Small" description="Serves 2." />
  <Radio value="large" label="Large" description="Serves 6." />
</RadioGroup>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Checkbox` inside a `CheckboxGroup` instead when several choices may be picked.

## Props

Type: `RadioProps`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement. Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | Supporting text under the label, read after it through `aria-describedby`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Disables this one radio; the arrow keys skip it. |
| `disabledReason` | `string` | Why this radio can't be picked now. Turns it off with `aria-disabled`: it stays focusable, picking does nothing, and the reason shows as its tooltip on hover and keyboard focus and is read as its description. The arrow keys skip it, as they skip a `disabled` radio; Tab reaches it, so a keyboard user can read why. It wins over `disabled`. Pass `undefined` while the radio is available. |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Hides the label visually; screen readers still read it as the radio's name. |
| `label` (required) | `string` | The choice's name, shown to the right of the radio. Required: every control needs a name. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | The radio element, a `<button role="radio">`, which the label names with `for`. |
| `value` (required) | `string` | What the group submits when this radio is picked, and the group's `value` then. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `checked`: Not a prop. The group's `value` picks the radio: `<RadioGroup value="small">`.
- `name`: Not a prop. The group's `name` applies to every radio: `<RadioGroup name="size">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
